title: Flatness over a filtered colimit of rings
statement: Let $\mathcal I$ be a small filtered category (for instance a directed set) and $i\mapsto R_i$ a functor from $\mathcal I$ to commutative rings with colimit $R=\varinjlim_iR_i$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] and coprojections $\iota_i:R_i\to R$. Let $\psi:R\to S$ be a ring map of commutative rings such that for every object $i$ the composite $\psi\circ\iota_i:R_i\to S$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Then $\psi$ is flat.

source.place: Lemma Tag 05UU (lemma-colimit-rings-flat, line 8857), part (1) with $M=S$ (stated for a directed set; the proof uses only that $\otimes$ commutes with colimits and that filtered colimits of modules are exact, Lemma Tag 00DB lemma-directed-colimit-exact; a filtered index category reduces to a directed set by Categories Lemma Tag 0032 categories-lemma-directed-category-system); cited in more-algebra.tex, proof of Lemma Tag 0AGV (line 3142)

proof.text: *Reduction to a directed set.* Since $\mathcal I$ is filtered, $\mathcal I^{\mathrm{op}}$ is cofiltered, and $(R,(\iota_i))$ is a limit of the opposite diagram $\mathcal I^{\mathrm{op}}\to(\text{commutative rings})^{\mathrm{op}}$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. By [lem-weil-pbc-cofiltered-limit-directed-reindex] there are a nonempty directed set $(A,\le)$, objects $i_a$ ($a\in A$) and morphisms $i_a\to i_b$ of $\mathcal I$ for $a\le b$, compatible with composition, such that $R$ with the maps $\iota_{i_a}$ is the colimit in commutative rings of the directed system $(R_{i_a})_{a\in A}$ with the induced transition maps. The hypothesis is about each $\psi\circ\iota_{i_a}$ separately, so it still holds. Hence we may and do assume that $\mathcal I$ is a nonempty directed set $I$, with transition maps $\varphi_{i'i}:R_i\to R_{i'}$ ($i\le i'$), so that $\iota_{i'}\circ\varphi_{i'i}=\iota_i$. Each $R_i$ acts on $S$ through $\psi\iota_i$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0032 (categories-lemma-directed-category-system); Algebra Lemma 05UU is stated for a directed set

proof.text: *Ideal criterion.* By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-fg-ideal-criterion] it suffices to show: for every finitely generated ideal $\mathfrak a\subset R$ the map $\mu:\mathfrak a\otimes_RS\to S$, $x\otimes s\mapsto\psi(x)s$, is injective.

source.place: Lemma Tag 05UU, proof: 'By Lemma lemma-flat [Tag 00HD] it suffices to show that $\mathfrak a\otimes_RM\to M$ is injective'

proof.text: *Descending the ideal to a stage.* Let $\mathfrak a=(r_1,\dots,r_n)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise] (2), applied with base ring $\mathbb Z$ (commutative rings are the commutative $\mathbb Z$-algebras), $r_k=\iota_{i_k}(y_k)$ with $y_k\in R_{i_k}$; choose $i_0\in I$ with $i_0\ge i_1,\dots,i_n$ and put $x_k=\varphi_{i_0i_k}(y_k)$, so $r_k=\iota_{i_0}(x_k)$. Let $J=\{j\in I:j\ge i_0\}$, a directed set; every $i\in I$ has some $j\in J$ with $j\ge i$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-initial-full-subcategory] (1) (with the cofiltered category $I^{\mathrm{op}}$ and its full subcategory $J^{\mathrm{op}}$) $R$ with the $\iota_j$, $j\in J$, is the colimit of $(R_j)_{j\in J}$ in commutative rings. For $j\in J$ let $\mathfrak a_j\subset R_j$ be the ideal generated by $\varphi_{ji_0}(x_1),\dots,\varphi_{ji_0}(x_n)$. Then $\varphi_{j'j}(\mathfrak a_j)\subset\mathfrak a_{j'}$ for $j\le j'$ in $J$, $\iota_j(\mathfrak a_j)\subset\mathfrak a$, and $\mathfrak a=\bigcup_{j\in J}\iota_j(\mathfrak a_j)$: an element $\sum_ks_kr_k$ ($s_k\in R$) has $s_k=\iota_j(t_k)$ for one $j\in J$ (again by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise] (2) and directedness), and then $\sum_ks_kr_k=\iota_j(\sum_kt_k\varphi_{ji_0}(x_k))$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 05UU, proof: 'We can find an $i\in I$ and a finitely generated ideal $\mathfrak a'\subset R_i$ such that $\mathfrak a=\mathfrak a'R$. Then $\mathfrak a=\colim_{i'\ge i}\mathfrak a'R_{i'}$'

proof.text: *$\mathfrak a$ and $R$ as colimits of abelian groups.* The groups $\mathfrak a_j$ ($j\in J$) with the restrictions of $\varphi_{j'j}$ form a directed system, and $\mathfrak a$ with the restrictions of the $\iota_j$ is its colimit in abelian groups [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]: given additive maps $g_j:\mathfrak a_j\to G$ with $g_{j'}\circ\varphi_{j'j}=g_j$, put $g(\iota_j(y))=g_j(y)$. This is well defined: if $\iota_j(y)=\iota_{j'}(y')$ with $y\in\mathfrak a_j$, $y'\in\mathfrak a_{j'}$, then by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-rings-zero] there is $k\ge j,j'$ with $\varphi_{kj}(y)=\varphi_{kj'}(y')$ in $\mathfrak a_k$, so $g_j(y)=g_k(\varphi_{kj}(y))=g_k(\varphi_{kj'}(y'))=g_{j'}(y')$. It is defined on all of $\mathfrak a$ by step 3, additive (bring two elements to a common stage), and unique since $\mathfrak a=\bigcup_j\iota_j(\mathfrak a_j)$. The same argument with $\mathfrak a_j$ replaced by $R_j$ (every element of $R$ comes from some $R_j$, $j\in J$, by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise] (2) and directedness) shows that $R$ with the $\iota_j$ is the colimit of $(R_j)_{j\in J}$ in abelian groups. The $R$-module structure that the colimit $\mathfrak a$ receives from the $R_j$-module structures of the $\mathfrak a_j$, $\iota_j(t)\cdot\iota_j(y)=\iota_j(ty)$, is multiplication in $R$, since $\iota_j$ is a ring map.

source.place: Lemma Tag 05UU, proof: 'Then $\mathfrak a=\colim_{i'\ge i}\mathfrak a'R_{i'}$' (the identification written out)

proof.text: *Tensor products commute with the colimit.* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-tensor-varying-rings] over the directed set $J$ with $A_j=R_j$ (colimit $A=R$, step 3), $M_j=\mathfrak a_j$ (colimit $M=\mathfrak a$ with its $R$-module structure, step 4) and $N_j=S$ for all $j$, with $R_j$ acting through $\psi\iota_j$ and transition maps $\mathrm{id}_S$; these are semilinear because $\psi\iota_{j'}\varphi_{j'j}=\psi\iota_j$. Since $J$ is nonempty and directed, hence connected, $S$ with the maps $\mathrm{id}_S$ is the colimit of this constant system [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-constant-connected-diagram], and the $R$-module structure it receives, $\iota_j(t)\cdot s=\psi(\iota_j(t))s$, is the one through $\psi$. So, with $T_j=\mathfrak a_j\otimes_{R_j}S$, transition maps $y\otimes s\mapsto\varphi_{j'j}(y)\otimes s$ and colimit $(T,(\lambda_j))$ in abelian groups, there is an isomorphism $\Psi:T\to\mathfrak a\otimes_RS$ with $\Psi(\lambda_j(y\otimes s))=\iota_j(y)\otimes s$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 05UU, proof: 'Since $\otimes$ commutes with colimits the map $\mathfrak a\otimes_RM\to M$ is the colimit of the maps $\mathfrak a'R_{i'}\otimes_{R_{i'}}M_{i'}\to M_{i'}$' (here $M_{i'}=S$; tensor products over the varying rings $R_{i'}$)

proof.text: *The maps at each stage are injective.* For $j\in J$ let $h_j:T_j\to S$, $y\otimes s\mapsto\psi(\iota_j(y))s$. It is the composite of $\mathfrak a_j\otimes_{R_j}S\to R_j\otimes_{R_j}S$ (the inclusion $\mathfrak a_j\subset R_j$ tensored with $S$), injective because $S$ is a flat $R_j$-module via $\psi\iota_j$ by hypothesis [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], with the isomorphism $R_j\otimes_{R_j}S\to S$, $t\otimes s\mapsto\psi(\iota_j(t))s$. So $h_j$ is injective, and $h_{j'}\circ(\varphi_{j'j}\otimes\mathrm{id})=h_j$ since $\iota_{j'}\varphi_{j'j}=\iota_j$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 05UU, proof: 'These maps are all injective by assumption'

proof.text: *Conclusion.* The sequences $0\to T_j\xrightarrow{h_j}S$ are exact at $T_j$ for every $j\in J$ and form a morphism of directed systems into the constant system $S$; since filtered colimits of abelian groups are exact [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-abelian-groups-exact], the induced map $h:T\to\varinjlim_JS=S$ (the colimit of the constant system being $S$ with the maps $\mathrm{id}_S$ [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-constant-connected-diagram]), characterized by $h\circ\lambda_j=h_j$, is injective. Now $\mu\circ\Psi=h$: both are additive and agree on the elements $\lambda_j(y\otimes s)$, which generate $T$ ($\mu(\Psi(\lambda_j(y\otimes s)))=\mu(\iota_j(y)\otimes s)=\psi(\iota_j(y))s=h_j(y\otimes s)$). As $\Psi$ is bijective (step 5), $\mu=h\circ\Psi^{-1}$ is injective. By step 2, $\psi$ is flat.
